Context  
At our enterprise, we migrated a monolithic application to a microservices architecture on Kubernetes, spanning AWS and GCP. The system’s complexity grew exponentially, with over 150 services, each exposing metrics via different endpoints. While Prometheus was already in use for some services, the lack of a unified observability layer led to fragmented visibility, making root cause analysis during outages a guessing game.  

Challenge  
The primary hurdle was reconciling disparate metrics from services using Prometheus exporters, Kubernetes metrics, and custom dashboards. Our existing setup relied on ad-hoc Grafana panels, which were inconsistent and lacked correlation between service health, infrastructure metrics, and business KPIs. During a recent incident, a 45-minute outage was traced to a misconfigured autoscaler in AWS, but the lack of contextual data delayed resolution. We needed a holistic view of the system’s state, from container-level metrics to cloud costs, without manual intervention.  

Solution  
We rearchitected observability around Prometheus as the central metric source, integrating Kubernetes metrics, custom exporters, and AWS/GCP cloud provider metrics via the CloudWatch and Stackdriver Prometheus exporters. Grafana became the unified visualization layer, with dashboards auto-generated using Prometheus’ remote write and Grafana’s templating capabilities. We leveraged Terraform to standardize Prometheus server configurations across clusters and used ArgoCD to sync Grafana dashboards across environments. Chaos engineering exercises were baked into the observability pipeline, simulating network partitions and resource exhaustion to validate alerting rules.  

Results  
Post-implementation, mean time to resolution (MTTR) for critical incidents dropped by 40%, and SLA compliance improved to 99.95%. The unified dashboard enabled correlation between service latency spikes and cloud cost anomalies, revealing a 12% overprovisioning in GCP compute instances. Automated alert suppression rules reduced noise by 65%, while Prometheus’ query language (PromQL) allowed teams to drill into root causes with custom queries.  

Lessons Learned  
Observability isn’t just about metrics—it’s about context. We learned to prioritize tooling that reduces friction, like using Prometheus’ service discovery to auto-instrument services without manual configuration. Collaboration between SRE, DevOps, and business teams was critical to align dashboards with KPIs. Lastly, observability is a moving target: we’ve since added custom metrics for API request latencies and integrated with GitLab CI for automated dashboard updates. The journey taught us that true observability requires as much architecture as it does tooling.
